newsitem.title: UK: 13th person dies in UK food poisoning outbreak.
newsitem.headline: 13th person dies in UK food poisoning outbreak.

text.p: A 13th person has died in Britain's worst outbreak of food poisoning, officials said on Tuesday.
A "frail and very elderly" woman died of the E coli strain of food poisoning at a Scottish nursing home near Glasgow, health officials said.

The 13 people who have died in one of the most serious cases of food poisoning ever recorded in the world have all been elderly. Most of the cases are linked to two Scottish butcher's shops -- one of which recently won awards for its products.

More than 300 people have reported symptoms of the food poisoning, which can cause kidney failure in vulnerable people such as the elderly and young children. Doctors have confirmed more than 200 cases but say the number has stabilised.
E coli is a bacteria normally found in the guts of cattle, sheep and people. It is usually harmless but one strain, known as 0157, can cause brain damage and kidney failure.
It gets into food via improper slaughtering techniques or through manure used as fertiliser.
The deadliest outbreak of E coli was in Canada, where 19 old people infected in a nursing home died in September 1985.
Eleven people, mostly schoolchildren, died in an outbreak in Japan in July and 9,500 became ill.
